basis: Thoracic/rib malformations and developmental disability define the syndrome; sustained restrictive respiratory insufficiency affects most patients (~80-90%).

decisions.pulmonary: involved: sustained restrictive respiratory insufficiency from congenital thoracic hypoplasia affects most patients (~80-90%).

basis: Neurodevelopmental, cutaneous and congenital cardiac abnormalities characterize the major RASopathies; cardiac lesions are defining features of Noonan-related syndromes.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital heart defects and cardiomyopathy are defining manifestations across major Noonan-related RASopathies, although less characteristic of NF1.

basis: Neurodevelopmental and sacral defects define syndrome; strabismus 8/12, myopia 4/7 and hearing loss 5/9. Aplasia cutis 5/10 omitted at cap; dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: dysphagia and constipation do not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal damage; swallowing dysfunction is attributable to neurologic impairment.
decisions.ocular: involved: strabismus in 8/12 and myopia in 4/7 establish common ocular dysfunction.

basis: Cerebellar malformation and corneal dystrophy define syndrome; hypospadias is a structural urethral defect in 30-79%. Renal cysts occur in only 5-29%.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias affects the urethra, explicitly included in the renal axis, and occurs in 30-79%; genital agenesis alone would not qualify.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic encephalomyopathy defines MELAS; sensorineural hearing loss occurs in roughly 40-60% of MELAS overall, with MTTK-specific prevalence uncertain.

decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing loss is common in the usual MELAS course (~40-60%); applying the syndrome phenotype to this rare genetic subtype is less certain.

basis: Intellectual disability and eye/skin anomalies define syndrome; structural jaw and toe abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Obesity and dental abnormalities omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none at cap: defining obesity occurs in 30-79%, but structural skeletal abnormalities receive the remaining slot based on direct organ impairment.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: hallux valgus, cone-shaped toe epiphyses and jaw abnormalities occur in 30-79%; retained within the four-axis cap.

basis: Glycosylation disorder with severe developmental delay in 9/9 and absent speech in 7/7. Cardiac, renal, ocular and pulmonary malformations have isolated reports without reliable prevalence.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: cardiac malformations have single-case annotations; 1/1 assessed does not establish prevalence of at least 30% across the reported disease population.
decisions.renal: none: renal dysplasia and hydronephrosis have single-case annotations; population prevalence of at least 30% is not established.

basis: Defined by disease of hormone-secreting neuroendocrine glands; neural regulation and ontology ancestry do not establish nervous-tissue disease across this umbrella.

decisions.neurologic: none: responding to neural stimuli does not establish nervous-tissue injury; neurologic disease is not shared across this broad gland-defined group.

basis: Hepatic heme-synthesis disorder defined by neurovisceral attacks; skin scarring occurs in 30-79% per HPO despite photosensitivity/blistering in 5-29%. Abdominal pain alone adds no GI axis.

decisions.neurologic: primary: neurovisceral attacks are part of the disease definition and reflect autonomic/neural dysfunction; the 5-29% motor-polyneuropathy frequency does not exclude this defining axis.

basis: Vibrio infections predominantly occupy the intestinal tract and cause enteric dysfunction, especially cholera; wound infection and septicemia characterize a smaller subset.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: intestinal infection is the predominant disease location across Vibrio infections, including cholera; it represents the infection site rather than a secondary complication.
